questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(a) Compared to many other organisms, bacteria as a group show the most extensive metabolic diversity.
(b) Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria use light energy to synthesise their food from inorganic substrates.
(c) Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in cell wall structure, and this feature is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.
(d) Methanogens are present in the gut of ruminants and help produce biogas from their dung.
(e) Thermoacidophiles are archaebacteria characteristically found in marshy areas.
questions.explanation:
(a) Correct: bacteria as a group show the most extensive metabolic diversity.
(b) Incorrect: chemosynthetic autotrophs get energy by oxidising inorganic substances such as nitrites and nitrates, not from light.
(c) Correct: the different cell wall structure of archaebacteria is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.
(d) Correct: methanogens live in the ruminant gut and help produce biogas from dung.
(e) Incorrect: thermoacidophiles live in hot springs, while methanogens occupy marshy areas.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sexual reproduction in members of Kingdom Protista involves:
options: Plasmogamy followed by a long dikaryophase
Transfer of DNA through a conjugation tube only
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: Protists are eukaryotes. They reproduce asexually, and sexually by a process involving cell fusion and zygote formation.
Option (2) states exactly this.
(1) Fission is an asexual method.
(3) Plasmogamy followed by a long dikaryophase is typical of ascomycete and basidiomycete fungi, not protists.
(4) Transfer of DNA through a conjugation tube describes bacterial conjugation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Albugo, the fungus that causes white spots on mustard leaves, belongs to which class of fungi?
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives Albugo, the parasitic fungus on mustard, as an example of Phycomycetes. Mucor and Rhizopus are listed in the same class.
The tempting wrong choice is Basidiomycetes, since it also contains plant parasites. However, its NCERT examples are rusts (Puccinia) and smuts (Ustilago), not Albugo.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (effect caused):
List-I
A. Trypanosoma
B. Plasmodium
C. Puccinia
D. Albugo
List-II
I. White spots on mustard leaves
II. Malaria
III. Sleeping sickness
IV. Wheat rust
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan that causes sleeping sickness, so A-III.
B. Plasmodium is a sporozoan that causes malaria, so B-II.
C. Puccinia, a basidiomycete, causes rust of wheat, so C-IV.
D. Albugo is a parasitic phycomycete that causes white rust (white spots) on mustard leaves, so D-I.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the five kingdom classification, Chlamydomonas and Amoeba are placed in the same kingdom, although earlier systems placed them in different kingdoms.
Reason (R): Both Chlamydomonas and Amoeba possess a cell wall.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Chlamydomonas and Amoeba are both unicellular eukaryotes, so Whittaker placed both in Protista. Earlier, walled Chlamydomonas went with plants (algae) and wall-less Amoeba went with animals.
R is false. Amoeba has no cell wall, and only Chlamydomonas has one. This difference is exactly why older systems separated them.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about viruses is correct?
options: Viruses that infect plants generally have double-stranded DNA as their genetic material
W.M. Stanley showed that crystallised viruses consist largely of nucleic acids
Some viruses contain both RNA and DNA in the same particle
Bacteriophages are usually double-stranded DNA viruses
questions.explanation:
(1) Wrong: Plant viruses generally have single-stranded RNA, not double-stranded DNA.
(2) Wrong: Stanley showed that virus crystals consist largely of proteins.
(3) Wrong: A virus contains either RNA or DNA, never both.
(4) Correct: Per NCERT, bacteriophages are usually double-stranded DNA viruses.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Viroids cause potato spindle tuber disease.
Reason (R): The RNA of a viroid is of low molecular weight.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In 1971, T.O. Diener found that an infectious agent smaller than a virus causes potato spindle tuber disease and named it a viroid.
R is true. The viroid is a free RNA without a protein coat, and its RNA is of low molecular weight.
However, the low molecular weight of the RNA is only a structural fact. It does not explain why viroids cause this disease, so R is not the correct explanation of A.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following organisms are protozoans?
Amoeba, Euglena, Gonyaulax, Trypanosoma, Plasmodium, Paramoecium, slime mould, Entamoeba
questions.explanation:
Protozoans in the list: Amoeba (amoeboid), Entamoeba (amoeboid), Trypanosoma (flagellated), Paramoecium (ciliated) and Plasmodium (sporozoan). That makes 5.
Not protozoans: Euglena is a euglenoid, Gonyaulax is a dinoflagellate, and slime moulds form a separate saprophytic group.
All eight organisms are protists, but only five are protozoans.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A microscope slide shows a marine, photosynthetic unicellular organism. Its outer surface is covered with stiff cellulose plates. It has two flagella: one runs lengthwise and the other lies crosswise in a groove between the plates. To which group does it belong?
questions.explanation:
Dinoflagellates are mostly marine, photosynthetic protists. Their cell wall carries stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface.
They have two flagella. One runs longitudinally, and the other lies transversely in a furrow between the wall plates. This matches the slide exactly.
The tempting wrong option is Euglenoids. They have no cell wall, only a flexible protein-rich pellicle, and their two flagella are short and long, not set in grooves.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Kingdom Protista is correct?
options: It includes all unicellular organisms, whether prokaryotic or eukaryotic
Its members lack membrane-bound organelles because they are single-celled
It groups together Chlamydomonas, which has a cell wall, and Paramoecium, which lacks one, although they were earlier placed in different kingdoms
Its members are primarily terrestrial and reproduce only asexually
questions.explanation:
Protista contains only single-celled eukaryotes. Chlamydomonas (walled, earlier placed with algae/plants) and Paramoecium (wall-less, earlier placed with animals) are now grouped together here. So (3) is correct.
(1) is wrong: prokaryotes belong to Monera.
(2) is wrong: protists are eukaryotes with a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
(4) is wrong: protists are primarily aquatic and reproduce both asexually and sexually.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A cavity called the gullet, which opens to the outside of the cell surface, is a characteristic feature of
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: ciliated protozoans such as Paramoecium have a gullet, a cavity that opens to the outside of the cell surface.
Coordinated beating of the cilia drives water laden with food into the gullet.
Amoeba feeds using pseudopodia instead, and Trypanosoma and Plasmodium have no gullet.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Agaricus
(B) Ustilago
(C) Puccinia
(D) Trichoderma
List-II
(I) Rust fungus
(II) Imperfect fungus
(III) Mushroom
(IV) Smut
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation:
A. Agaricus is a mushroom, so A matches III.
B. Ustilago is the smut fungus, so B matches IV.
C. Puccinia is the rust fungus, so C matches I.
D. Trichoderma is a deuteromycete, or imperfect fungus, so D matches II.
The correct sequence is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II. Option (2) is the trap because it swaps rust and smut.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which group of protozoans moves and captures prey by putting out pseudopodia (false feet)?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: amoeboid protozoans, such as Amoeba, move and capture prey by putting out pseudopodia (false feet).
The other groups move differently. Flagellates use flagella, and ciliates use cilia. Sporozoans have no specific locomotory structures.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Methanogens in the gut of ruminants such as cows and buffaloes produce methane (biogas) from their dung.
Statement II: Archaebacteria have a cell wall structure different from other bacteria, and this helps them survive in extreme conditions.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT states that methanogens in the gut of ruminants like cows and buffaloes are responsible for producing methane (biogas) from their dung.
Statement II is correct. Archaebacteria have a cell wall structure different from other bacteria, and NCERT says this feature allows them to survive in extreme habitats such as hot springs, salty areas and marshes.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (fungus) with List-II (feature/importance):
List-I
A. Yeast
B. Puccinia
C. Penicillium
D. Albugo
List-II
I. Source of antibiotics
II. Parasite on mustard
III. Used in making bread and beer
IV. Causes wheat rust
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. Yeast is used in making bread and beer, so A–III.
B. Puccinia causes wheat rust, so B–IV.
C. Penicillium is a source of antibiotics, so C–I.
D. Albugo is a parasite on mustard, so D–II.
Only option (1) gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in the life of a slime mould in the correct order:
P. Plasmodium differentiates to form fruiting bodies
Q. Walled spores are dispersed by air currents
R. Cells aggregate to form a plasmodium under suitable conditions
S. Body moves along decaying twigs and leaves, engulfing organic material
questions.explanation:
S comes first: the slime mould feeds saprophytically, moving over decaying twigs and leaves and engulfing organic matter.
R comes next: under suitable conditions the cells aggregate into a plasmodium.
P follows: when conditions turn unfavourable, the plasmodium differentiates into fruiting bodies.
Q comes last: the walled spores from the fruiting bodies are dispersed by air currents.
The order is S → R → P → Q.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fungal hyphae that are continuous tubes without cross walls and are filled with multinucleated cytoplasm are called:
questions.explanation:
Coenocytic hyphae are continuous tubes with no septa (cross walls), so their cytoplasm is multinucleate.
Septate hyphae do have cross walls.
Dikaryotic hyphae have cells that each contain two nuclei.
Conidiophores are hyphae that bear conidia (asexual spores).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about protists is incorrect?
options: Euglenoids have a protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall, which makes the body flexible
The spores formed by slime moulds lack true walls and are therefore short-lived
In most dinoflagellates, one flagellum lies longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the wall plates
Rapid multiplication of Gonyaulax can make the sea appear red
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. Euglenoids have a protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall, which makes the body flexible.
(2) Incorrect. Slime mould spores do have true walls. They are extremely resistant and can survive for many years in unfavourable conditions.
(3) Correct. In most dinoflagellates, one flagellum lies longitudinally and the other lies transversely in a furrow between the wall plates.
(4) Correct. Rapid multiplication of Gonyaulax causes red tides, making the sea look red.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cell walls of fungi are mainly composed of:
options: Silica embedded in two overlapping shells
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: fungal cell walls are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.
This is one reason fungi are kept separate from plants, whose walls are cellulosic.
The other options belong to different groups:
(1) Cellulose and pectin: plants.
(3) Silica in two overlapping shells: diatoms.
(4) Polysaccharides with amino acids: Monera (bacteria).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
A. Ivanowsky (1892)
B. Beijerinck (1898)
C. Stanley (1935)
D. Diener (1971)
List-II:
I. Showed viruses can be crystallised and the crystals are largely protein
II. Discovered a coat-less infectious RNA causing potato spindle tuber disease
III. Found that the agent of tobacco mosaic disease passes through bacteria-proof filters
IV. Showed sap of infected plants infects healthy plants and named it Contagium vivum fluidum
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A–III: Ivanowsky (1892) found that the tobacco mosaic agent passes through bacteria-proof filters, so it is smaller than bacteria.
B–IV: Beijerinck (1898) showed that the sap of infected plants infects healthy plants and called it Contagium vivum fluidum.
C–I: Stanley (1935) showed that viruses can be crystallised and that the crystals are largely protein.
D–II: Diener (1971) discovered the viroid, a coat-less RNA that causes potato spindle tuber disease.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Compared to many other organisms, bacteria as a group show the most extensive metabolic diversity.
Statement II: All autotrophic bacteria synthesise their food by photosynthesis.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT notes that bacteria as a group show the most extensive metabolic diversity.
Statement II is incorrect. Autotrophic bacteria may be photosynthetic, like cyanobacteria.
They may also be chemosynthetic, oxidising inorganic substances such as ammonia, nitrites and nitrates to obtain energy.
So not all autotrophic bacteria photosynthesise.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A unicellular, wall-less eukaryote is observed in pond water. Based on NCERT, which one of the following observations would rule out placing it among the protozoans?
options: It extends pseudopodia to engulf smaller organisms
It carries out photosynthesis when exposed to sunlight
It has an infectious spore-like stage in its life cycle
It lives as a parasite inside another organism
questions.explanation:
Key fact: all protozoans are heterotrophs, so a protozoan never photosynthesises.
(1) Pseudopodia are used by amoeboid protozoans, so this fits a protozoan.
(3) An infectious spore-like stage is the defining feature of sporozoans.
(4) Parasitism is seen in Entamoeba, Trypanosoma and Plasmodium.
(2) Photosynthesis in sunlight excludes the organism from protozoans. It points instead to a euglenoid such as Euglena.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A symbiotic association between a fungus and the roots of higher plants is known as:
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: a fungus living in association with the roots of higher plants forms mycorrhiza.
The tempting wrong option is lichen. A lichen is a fungus associated with algae, not with roots.
Mycelium is just the network of fungal hyphae.
Plasmodium is the aggregation of slime moulds.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a lichen, the algal partner is called the ______ and its mode of nutrition is ______.
questions.explanation:
A lichen is a mutually useful association between an alga and a fungus.
The algal partner is the phycobiont. It contains chlorophyll and is autotrophic, so it makes food for both partners.
The fungal partner is the mycobiont. It is heterotrophic and provides shelter and absorbs mineral nutrients and water.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A bacterium seen under the microscope is shaped like a comma. Into which shape category would it be placed?
questions.explanation:
Bacteria are grouped by shape into four types.
Coccus means spherical, bacillus means rod-shaped, vibrio means comma-shaped and spirillum means spiral.
A comma-shaped bacterium is therefore a vibrio.
Spirillum is the tempting wrong option, but it is fully coiled. A comma shows only a single slight curve.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Associations between Mycobiont and Phycobiont are found in
questions.explanation:
Lichens are symbiotic associations between algae and fungi.
The algal partner is called the phycobiont. It prepares food by photosynthesis.
The fungal partner is called the mycobiont. It provides shelter and absorbs minerals and water.
Mycorrhiza fails because it is fungus plus plant root, with no alga involved.
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 2 (MCQ Q8)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following organisms completely lacks a cell wall?
questions.explanation:
Mycoplasma are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen.
Anabaena and Nostoc are cyanobacteria (eubacteria) with a cell wall.
Methanogens are archaebacteria. They have a cell wall too, though its structure differs from that of eubacteria.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about protozoans is incorrect?
options: Marine amoeboid protozoans bear silica shells on their surface
In ciliated protozoans, coordinated beating of rows of cilia steers water laden with food into the gullet
Sporozoans move actively with thousands of cilia and have an infectious spore-like stage
Parasitic flagellated protozoans can cause diseases such as sleeping sickness
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: marine amoeboid protozoans have silica shells on their surface.
(2) Correct: in ciliates such as Paramoecium, coordinated beating of rows of cilia sends food-laden water into the gullet.
(3) Incorrect: sporozoans such as Plasmodium are defined by an infectious spore-like stage. Having thousands of cilia is a feature of ciliates.
(4) Correct: Trypanosoma is a parasitic flagellate that causes sleeping sickness.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following gives the correct sequence of events in the sexual cycle of fungi?
questions.explanation:
Step 1, plasmogamy: the protoplasms of two motile or non-motile gametes fuse.
Step 2, karyogamy: the two haploid nuclei fuse to form a diploid zygote.
Step 3, meiosis: meiosis in the zygote produces haploid spores.
Option (1) wrongly puts karyogamy first. Nuclei cannot fuse before the protoplasts have fused.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cell walls of diatoms are embedded with which substance, which makes them practically indestructible?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: diatom cell walls form two thin overlapping shells embedded with silica. This makes them practically indestructible.
Because the walls do not decay, they pile up over millions of years and form 'diatomaceous earth'.
Option (1), cellulose, is the tempting wrong choice. Cellulose plates form the walls of dinoflagellates, not diatoms.
Option (3), chitin, is found in fungal cell walls.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Slime moulds move along decaying twigs and leaves, engulfing organic material. Their mode of nutrition is best described as:
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes slime moulds as saprophytic protists. They move along decaying twigs and leaves and engulf the organic material.
They have no photosynthetic pigments, so they are not photosynthetic autotrophs.
They cannot oxidise inorganic substances, so they are not chemosynthetic.
They feed on dead matter rather than living hosts, so they are not parasitic.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The infectious agent discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971, which is smaller than viruses, causes which disease?
questions.explanation:
In 1971, T.O. Diener discovered the viroid. It is a free, low molecular weight RNA that lacks a protein coat, and it causes potato spindle tuber disease.
The other diseases have different causes: tobacco mosaic disease is caused by a virus, citrus canker by a bacterium, and BSE by a prion.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are correct for Deuteromycetes?
(a) Mycelium is septate and branched
(b) Reproduction occurs only by asexual spores called conidia
(c) A large number are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling
(d) Sexual spores are produced in ascocarps
(e) Mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic
questions.explanation:
(a) Correct: the mycelium is septate and branched.
(b) Correct: they reproduce only by asexual spores called conidia.
(c) Correct: many are decomposers of litter and help in mineral cycling.
(d) Incorrect: ascocarps and ascospores belong to ascomycetes. The sexual stage of deuteromycetes is not known.
(e) Incorrect: aseptate, coenocytic mycelium is a feature of phycomycetes.
So three features are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What character did Aristotle use to divide animals into two groups?
options: Presence or absence of a backbone
Presence or absence of red blood
questions.explanation:
Aristotle divided animals into two groups: those with red blood and those without red blood.
The tempting option is the backbone, i.e. vertebrates versus invertebrates. That grouping was introduced much later and was not Aristotle's criterion.
Flying ability and habitat were never his basis for the two-group division.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Earlier systems grouped bacteria, blue-green algae, fungi, mosses, ferns, gymnosperms and angiosperms together as 'Plants' because all had a cell wall. Which pair from this old grouping was split into different Whittaker kingdoms solely because one member is unicellular and the other multicellular? (Both members are eukaryotic, photosynthetic and walled.)
questions.explanation:
Chlamydomonas and Spirogyra are both eukaryotic, photosynthetic, walled green algae. Chlamydomonas is unicellular and goes to Protista. Spirogyra is multicellular and goes to Plantae.
Nostoc and Spirogyra: separated by prokaryotic versus eukaryotic cells.
Mucor and a fern: they differ in nutrition and wall material (chitin versus cellulose).
Chlorella and Chlamydomonas: both unicellular, so both stay in Protista and are not split.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a fungus, the long, slender thread-like structures that make up the body are collectively organised into a network. What is this network called?
questions.explanation:
The fungal body is made of long, slender threads, and each single thread is called a hypha.
The network formed by these hyphae is called the mycelium.
'Hypha' is the tempting wrong option, but it names one thread, not the whole network.
Plasmodium is the aggregation formed by slime moulds, and the pellicle is the protein-rich layer of euglenoids.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In basidiomycetes, karyogamy and meiosis take place in which structure?
questions.explanation:
Key fact (NCERT): In basidiomycetes, the dikaryotic mycelium forms club-shaped basidia. Karyogamy and then meiosis take place inside the basidium.
The basidium then produces four basidiospores, so option (2) fits.
Ascus is the tempting wrong option. It is where karyogamy and meiosis occur in ascomycetes, not basidiomycetes.
Sporangium and conidiophore are asexual spore-bearing structures.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Naked cytoplasm, multinucleated and saprophytic are the characteristics of
questions.explanation:
Slime moulds are saprophytic protists.
Under suitable conditions they aggregate into a plasmodium. This is a multinucleate mass of protoplasm with no cell wall, i.e. naked cytoplasm.
Fungi fail because they have chitin cell walls.
Monera fail because they are prokaryotes with no true nucleus.
Protista is too broad, since most protists are uninucleate. Slime moulds are the specific group that matches all three features.
Answer: (4)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 2 (MCQ Q4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Diatoms have left behind huge deposits of their cell walls over billions of years, forming 'diatomaceous earth'. Which property of their cell wall makes this possible?
options: The walls are made of chitin, which resists microbial digestion
The walls are embedded with silica, which makes them practically indestructible
The walls consist of stiff cellulose plates that are shed regularly
The walls are replaced by a protein-rich pellicle that fossilises easily
questions.explanation:
Diatom cell walls form two thin overlapping shells that fit together like a soap box.
These walls are embedded with silica, so they are practically indestructible. Over billions of years they accumulate as diatomaceous earth.
Option (3) is tempting but wrong: stiff cellulose plates are found in dinoflagellates.
The pellicle in (4) belongs to euglenoids, and chitin in (1) is a fungal wall material.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Euglena, the cell wall is absent. Which structure covers the body instead?
options: A cellulose wall made of stiff plates
A silica shell of two overlapping halves
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: euglenoids lack a cell wall. Instead, a protein-rich layer called the pellicle covers the body and keeps it flexible.
Option (1) fails because stiff cellulose plates are found in dinoflagellates.
Option (3) fails because a silica shell of two overlapping halves is the diatom 'soap box'.
Option (4) fails because chitin walls are typical of fungi.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cell wall of fungi is mainly composed of:
questions.explanation:
Fungal cell walls are made of chitin and polysaccharides (NCERT).
Cellulose walls are typical of plants.
A wall of polysaccharide plus amino acid (peptidoglycan) is typical of Monera.
Walls with embedded silica belong to diatoms.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In every fungus, the fusion of two compatible haploid cells immediately results in a diploid cell.
Statement II: Fungi form fruiting bodies in which reduction division occurs, leading to the formation of haploid spores.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. In some fungi, fusion of two haploid cells gives a diploid cell at once. In ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, an intervening dikaryotic (n + n) stage comes first, and karyogamy happens later.
Statement II is correct. Fungi form fruiting bodies in which reduction division (meiosis) occurs, producing haploid spores.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A diagram shows a virus with a polyhedral head, a collar, a sheath and tail fibres. It is being compared with a rod-shaped virus that causes mosaic disease in tobacco. Which statement correctly describes the first virus?
options: It is a plant virus with single-stranded RNA wound inside a helical capsid
It infects bacteria and usually carries double-stranded DNA protected by a capsid made of capsomeres
It is an infectious agent made only of abnormally folded protein
It is a free RNA molecule without any protein coat
questions.explanation:
A polyhedral head with a collar, sheath and tail fibres is the typical structure of a bacteriophage, a virus that infects bacteria.
Bacteriophages usually contain double-stranded DNA. It is protected by a capsid built from protein subunits called capsomeres.
Option (1) describes TMV, the rod-shaped plant virus.
Option (3) describes a prion.
Option (4) describes a viroid.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the flagella of a typical euglenoid?
options: One flagellum lying in a transverse furrow
Two flagella, one short and one long
Thousands of short flagella arranged in rows
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: euglenoids bear two flagella of unequal length, one short and one long.
Option (1) fails because a flagellum lying in a transverse furrow is a dinoflagellate feature.
Option (2) fails because equal flagella are not described for euglenoids.
Option (4) fails because rows of many short hair-like structures describe cilia in ciliates such as *Paramecium*.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which feature correctly describes Mycoplasma?
options: They have a rigid cell wall and a single flagellum
They are the largest prokaryotic cells and are strictly aerobic
They completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known
They are photosynthetic and contain chlorophyll a
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen.
So option (3) is correct.
Option (1) fails because a rigid cell wall is a feature of eubacteria, not Mycoplasma.
Option (2) is wrong on both counts. Mycoplasma are the smallest cells, not the largest, and they are not strictly aerobic.
Option (4) fails because Mycoplasma are not photosynthetic.
Answer: (4) is not it; the key is (3).
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about spore formation in fungi is INCORRECT?
options: In ascomycetes, conidia are produced exogenously on conidiophores
In ascomycetes, ascospores are produced endogenously in asci
In basidiomycetes, basidiospores are produced endogenously inside the basidium
In phycomycetes, zoospores and aplanospores are produced endogenously in a sporangium
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: in ascomycetes, conidia form exogenously on conidiophores.
(2) Correct: ascospores form endogenously inside sac-like asci.
(3) Incorrect: basidiospores form exogenously on the basidium, usually four per basidium. They are not formed inside it.
(4) Correct: in phycomycetes, zoospores and aplanospores form endogenously in a sporangium.
The question asks for the incorrect statement, so (3) is the choice.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (Kingdom) with List-II (Body organisation as given in the five kingdom comparison).
List-I:
(A) Monera
(B) Fungi
(C) Plantae
(D) Animalia
List-II:
(I) Tissue/organ
(II) Cellular
(III) Tissue/organ/organ system
(IV) Multicellular/loose tissue
questions.explanation:
NCERT's five kingdom comparison table gives each kingdom's body organisation.
(A) Monera: cellular (II).
(B) Fungi: multicellular or loose tissue (IV).
(C) Plantae: tissue or organ level (I).
(D) Animalia: tissue, organ or organ system level (III). Only animals reach the organ system level.
Option (4) is the trap because it swaps the plant and animal levels.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following spore types are produced during asexual reproduction in fungi?
Conidia, Oospores, Sporangiospores, Ascospores, Zoospores, Basidiospores
questions.explanation:
Asexual spores in fungi: conidia, sporangiospores and zoospores.
Sexual spores in fungi: oospores, ascospores and basidiospores.
So three of the listed spore types are asexual.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about acellular infectious agents:
I. Viruses infecting plants generally have single-stranded RNA, whereas bacteriophages are usually double-stranded DNA viruses.
II. The viroid causing potato spindle tuber disease is a free RNA of high molecular weight enclosed in a capsid.
III. Prions are abnormally folded proteins, similar in size to viruses, that cause certain neurological diseases.
IV. Some animal viruses contain both DNA and RNA as genetic material.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
I. Correct: NCERT states that plant viruses generally have single-stranded RNA, while bacteriophages usually have double-stranded DNA.
II. Incorrect: The potato spindle tuber viroid is free RNA with no protein coat (capsid). Its RNA is also of low, not high, molecular weight.
III. Correct: Prions are abnormally folded proteins, similar in size to viruses. They cause neurological diseases such as BSE (mad cow disease) and CJD.
IV. Incorrect: A virus carries either DNA or RNA as its genetic material, never both.
Only I and III are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are spores produced by sexual reproduction in fungi?
Conidia, Oospores, Ascospores, Sporangiospores, Basidiospores, Zoospores
questions.explanation:
Sexual spores of fungi: oospores (Phycomycetes), ascospores (Ascomycetes) and basidiospores (Basidiomycetes).
Asexual spores of fungi: conidia, sporangiospores and zoospores.
So three of the listed spores are sexual.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Entamoeba is an amoeboid protozoan that lives as a parasite.
Statement II: All flagellated protozoans are parasitic.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I: correct. NCERT gives Entamoeba as an example of a parasitic amoeboid protozoan.
Statement II: incorrect. Flagellated protozoans may be free-living or parasitic, so not all of them are parasites. Trypanosoma is a parasitic example.
So Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Lichens are generally not found growing in areas with heavy air pollution.
Reason (R): In a lichen, the mycobiont prepares food for the phycobiont, while the phycobiont absorbs water and minerals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Lichens are very sensitive to SO$_2$ and other pollutants, so they do not grow in polluted areas. This makes them good pollution indicators.
R is false because it swaps the roles of the partners.
The algal partner (phycobiont) is autotrophic and makes food for the fungus.
The fungal partner (mycobiont) gives shelter and absorbs water and mineral nutrients for the alga.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are characteristic features of Kingdom Animalia as described in NCERT?
(i) Multicellular organisation
(ii) Cells lack cell walls
(iii) Food is digested in an internal cavity
(iv) A definite growth pattern leading to adults of definite shape and size
(v) Alternation of haploid and diploid generations in the life cycle
(vi) Food reserves stored as starch
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: animals are multicellular eukaryotes.
(ii) Correct: animal cells lack cell walls.
(iii) Correct: food is digested in an internal cavity (holozoic nutrition).
(iv) Correct: growth follows a definite pattern, giving adults of definite shape and size.
(v) Incorrect: alternation of haploid and diploid generations is a feature of plants.
(vi) Incorrect: animals store food as glycogen or fat, not starch.
So four features fit.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A prokaryote is isolated from the rumen of a buffalo. It produces a combustible gas from ingested plant material. Which of the following best describes this organism?
options: A cyanobacterium that fixes nitrogen in heterocysts and releases the gas as a by-product
A thermoacidophile whose acid tolerance allows it to live in the rumen
A chemosynthetic autotroph that oxidises nitrites to release the gas
A methanogen, an archaebacterium with a cell wall structure distinct from eubacteria, also found in marshy areas
questions.explanation:
The combustible gas produced from plant material in a ruminant's gut is methane (biogas).
Methane-producing prokaryotes are methanogens. They are archaebacteria with a distinctive cell wall structure, and they also live in marshy areas.
Option (2) fails because thermoacidophiles live in hot springs, not in the rumen.
Options (1) and (3) fail because cyanobacteria and chemosynthetic bacteria are eubacteria and do not produce methane.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The mycelium of members of Phycomycetes is best described as:
options: Branched and septate with clamp connections
questions.explanation:
In Phycomycetes, the mycelium is aseptate, meaning the hyphae have no cross walls. The result is a continuous multinucleate tube, which is called coenocytic.
Septate mycelium is found in ascomycetes, basidiomycetes and deuteromycetes.
Dikaryotic cells and clamp connections are features of basidiomycetes, so options (1), (3) and (4) do not fit.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In basidiomycetes, basidiospores are produced endogenously inside the basidium.
Statement II: In basidiomycetes, asexual spores are generally not found, but vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Basidiospores are produced exogenously, on the outer surface of the basidium. Endogenous formation is a feature of ascospores in asci.
Statement II is correct. NCERT notes that asexual spores are generally not found in basidiomycetes, while vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common.
So Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Contagium vivum fluidum was proposed by
questions.explanation:
In 1892, Ivanowsky found that the agent of tobacco mosaic disease could pass through bacteria-proof filters.
Later, M.W. Beijerinck (1898) showed that the extract of infected tobacco plants could infect healthy plants.
He called this infectious fluid 'contagium vivum fluidum'.
Ivanowsky is the tempting wrong option because he did the earlier filtration work, but he did not coin the term.
Stanley crystallised the virus and showed it is mainly protein.
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 2 (MCQ Q7)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Aristotle made one of the earliest attempts at a scientific classification of plants. Into which groups did he divide them?
questions.explanation:
Aristotle was among the first to classify plants on a scientific basis. He used simple morphological characters such as overall growth form.
On this basis he divided plants into trees, shrubs and herbs.
The other groupings came much later. Monocot/dicot and flowering/non-flowering splits belong to later systems, and algae, fungi and mosses are modern categories.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (fungus) with List-II (class):
List-I:
A. Albugo
B. Neurospora
C. Ustilago
D. Trichoderma
List-II:
I. Deuteromycetes
II. Basidiomycetes
III. Phycomycetes
IV. Ascomycetes
questions.explanation:
A. Albugo, the parasite causing white rust of mustard, is a phycomycete (III).
B. Neurospora is an ascomycete (IV) used in genetic studies.
C. Ustilago, the smut fungus, is a basidiomycete (II).
D. Trichoderma has no known sexual stage, so it is a deuteromycete or imperfect fungus (I).
This gives A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In basidiomycetes such as Agaricus, karyogamy and meiosis take place in the basidium, producing four basidiospores.
Statement II: In basidiomycetes, the basidiospores are produced endogenously inside the basidium, and the basidia are arranged in fruiting bodies called basidiocarps.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In Agaricus, karyogamy and meiosis occur in the basidium and produce four basidiospores.
Statement II is incorrect. Basidiospores are produced exogenously, on the outside of the basidium. Endogenous spore formation in a sac (the ascus) is typical of ascomycetes. The part about basidia being arranged in basidiocarps is true, but the 'endogenous' claim makes the whole statement wrong.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are members of Ascomycetes?
Penicillium, Mucor, Aspergillus, Albugo, Claviceps, Agaricus, Neurospora, yeast
questions.explanation:
Ascomycetes (sac fungi) form sexual ascospores inside asci.
Ascomycetes: Penicillium, Aspergillus, Claviceps, Neurospora and yeast (Saccharomyces). That makes 5.
Not ascomycetes: Mucor and Albugo are phycomycetes (aseptate, coenocytic mycelium). Agaricus (mushroom) is a basidiomycete.
Total = 5.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: With respect to mode of nutrition, all protozoans are
options: Photosynthetic in light and heterotrophic in darkness
Heterotrophs living as predators or parasites
questions.explanation:
Key NCERT fact: all protozoans are heterotrophs. They live either as predators or as parasites.
They do not photosynthesise. They also do not carry out chemosynthesis, so options (1) and (2) are ruled out.
The tempting option (3) describes euglenoids such as Euglena. Euglena is photosynthetic in sunlight and behaves like a heterotroph, preying on smaller organisms, when light is absent. That makes it a euglenoid, not a protozoan.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Halophiles
B. Thermoacidophiles
C. Methanogens
D. Vibrio
List-II
I. Comma-shaped bacteria
II. Hot springs
III. Marshy areas
IV. Extremely salty areas
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A. Halophiles live in extremely salty areas, so A–IV.
B. Thermoacidophiles live in hot springs, so B–II.
C. Methanogens live in marshy areas, so C–III.
D. Vibrio is the comma-shaped form of bacteria, so D–I.
Watch for the trap of swapping the habitats of halophiles and thermoacidophiles.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bacteria show great metabolic diversity. Which nutritional group includes the vast majority of bacteria?
options: Organisms that switch between autotrophy and heterotrophy depending on light
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: some bacteria are photosynthetic or chemosynthetic autotrophs, but the vast majority are heterotrophs.
Heterotrophic bacteria depend on other organisms or on dead organic matter for food.
Option (4) is the tempting trap. Switching between autotrophy and heterotrophy depending on light describes euglenoids, which are protists, not bacteria.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Kingdom Fungi is INCORRECT?
options: Coenocytic hyphae have cross walls that divide the cytoplasm into uninucleate compartments
Except for unicellular forms such as yeast, fungi have a filamentous body made of hyphae
In ascomycetes, the nuclear condition during the sexual cycle changes in the order n → n + n → 2n → n
Reduction division in fungi occurs in fruiting bodies, leading to the formation of haploid spores
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: Coenocytic hyphae are continuous tubes of multinucleate cytoplasm with no septa. Cross walls belong to septate hyphae.
(2) Correct: Apart from unicellular yeasts, fungi have a filamentous body made of hyphae.
(3) Correct: In ascomycetes, plasmogamy gives a dikaryon ($n + n$). Karyogamy then makes it diploid ($2n$), and meiosis restores $n$.
(4) Correct: Meiosis takes place in the fruiting bodies and produces haploid spores.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: A viroid differs from a virus in lacking a protein coat, and its RNA is of low molecular weight.
Statement II: Prions, like viroids, are free nucleic acid molecules without a protein coat, and they cause neurological diseases such as BSE.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. A viroid is a free RNA of low molecular weight and has no protein coat, while a virus has a capsid.
Statement II is incorrect. A prion contains no nucleic acid at all. It is an abnormally folded protein, similar in size to a virus.
It is true that prions cause BSE (mad cow disease) and CJD, but the statement describes the agent wrongly.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The two kingdom system of Linnaeus' time did not distinguish between prokaryotes and eukaryotes, or between unicellular and multicellular organisms.
Statement II: The two kingdom system kept the photosynthetic green algae and the non-photosynthetic fungi in separate kingdoms.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The two kingdom system (Plantae and Animalia) did not separate prokaryotes from eukaryotes, unicellular from multicellular organisms, or photosynthetic from non-photosynthetic organisms.
Statement II is incorrect. The system did not keep them separate: it placed both photosynthetic green algae and non-photosynthetic fungi in the same kingdom, Plantae. This was a major drawback of the system.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about eubacteria is INCORRECT?
options: Cyanobacteria may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous, and their colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath
Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria help recycle nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur
Sexual reproduction in bacteria involves the fusion of male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote
Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission and may form spores under unfavourable conditions
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: cyanobacteria may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous, and their colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath.
(2) Correct: chemosynthetic autotrophs help recycle nitrogen, phosphorus, iron and sulphur.
(3) Incorrect: bacteria show only a sort of sexual reproduction, in which DNA is transferred in a primitive way from one bacterium to another. There is no fusion of gametes and no zygote. Gamete fusion and zygote formation are described for protists, not bacteria.
(4) Correct: bacteria reproduce mainly by fission and may form spores under unfavourable conditions.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the main criteria used by R.H. Whittaker (1969) in his Five Kingdom Classification?
options: Presence or absence of red blood
questions.explanation:
Whittaker's five kingdom classification (1969) used these main criteria: cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.
Cell structure, mode of nutrition and phylogenetic relationships are all on this list.
Presence or absence of red blood was Aristotle's character for dividing animals. It was not used by Whittaker.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Nostoc
(B) Mycoplasma
(C) Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria
(D) Heterotrophic bacteria
List-II
(I) Oxidise ammonia, nitrites and nitrates to obtain energy for ATP production
(II) Used in making curd from milk
(III) Heterocysts present
(IV) No cell wall at all
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(A) Nostoc: it is a filamentous cyanobacterium with heterocysts for nitrogen fixation, so A matches III.
(B) Mycoplasma: it has no cell wall at all, so B matches IV.
(C) Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria: they oxidise inorganic substances such as ammonia, nitrites and nitrates and use the energy to make ATP, so C matches I.
(D) Heterotrophic bacteria: they are used to make curd from milk, so D matches II.
The correct set is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Kingdom Protista brings together Chlamydomonas and Paramoecium, which were placed in different kingdoms in earlier classification systems.
Reason (R): Both Chlamydomonas and Paramoecium lack a cell wall, so they could not have been placed under plants.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
Assertion: True. Earlier systems placed Chlamydomonas, a unicellular green alga, under plants and Paramoecium, a protozoan, under animals. Whittaker's Kingdom Protista brings all single-celled eukaryotes together, so both now fall in Protista.
Reason: False. Chlamydomonas has a cellulose cell wall. Only Paramoecium lacks a wall; it has a flexible pellicle instead.
A false R cannot explain A. Options (1) and (2) need R to be true, so they are ruled out.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (protozoan group) with List-II (example):
List-I
A. Amoeboid protozoan
B. Flagellated protozoan
C. Ciliated protozoan
D. Sporozoan
List-II
I. Plasmodium
II. Paramoecium
III. Entamoeba
IV. Trypanosoma
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. Amoeboid protozoan: Entamoeba, a parasitic amoeboid form. A–III.
B. Flagellated protozoan: Trypanosoma, which causes sleeping sickness. B–IV.
C. Ciliated protozoan: Paramoecium, which moves with thousands of cilia. C–II.
D. Sporozoan: Plasmodium, the malarial parasite with an infectious spore-like stage. D–I.
This gives A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a unicellular fungus used in making bread and beer?
questions.explanation:
Most fungi are filamentous, but yeasts are unicellular.
Yeasts are used to make bread and beer.
Puccinia, Penicillium and Albugo are all filamentous fungi with hyphae. Penicillium is tempting because it is economically useful, but it is a source of antibiotics, not a baking or brewing agent.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Viroids are free RNA molecules of low molecular weight that lack a protein coat.
Statement II: Prions are abnormally folded proteins that are much smaller than viroids.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Viroids are free RNA molecules of low molecular weight with no protein coat. T.O. Diener discovered them as the cause of potato spindle tuber disease.
Statement II is incorrect. Prions are abnormally folded proteins, but NCERT says they are similar in size to viruses. They are not smaller than viroids.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Members of phycomycetes are found in
i. Aquatic habitats
ii. On decaying wood
iii. Moist and damp places
iv. As obligate parasites on plants
Choose from the following options
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that phycomycetes are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist and damp places, or as obligate parasites on plants.
(i) Correct: aquatic habitats are listed.
(ii) Correct: they grow on decaying wood.
(iii) Correct: they need moist, damp places.
(iv) Correct: they occur as obligate parasites on plants, e.g. Albugo.
All four statements are true.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The cell walls of diatoms are embedded with silica, so they are practically indestructible.
Statement II: Diatomaceous earth is gritty and is used in polishing and in the filtration of oils and syrups.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Diatom cell walls are embedded with silica, so they are practically indestructible. Over billions of years they have piled up as diatomaceous earth.
Statement II is correct. Diatomaceous earth is gritty, so it is used in polishing and in filtering oils and syrups.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Organisms living in salty areas are called as
questions.explanation:
Archaebacteria live in extreme habitats.
Halophiles live in extremely salty areas.
Thermoacidophiles live in hot springs.
Methanogens live in marshy areas and in the guts of ruminants, where they produce methane.
Heliophytes are sun-loving plants, not salt-dwelling organisms.
So organisms of salty areas are halophiles.
Answer: (2)
