questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, plasmogamy between two compatible haploid hyphae is immediately followed by karyogamy, giving diploid cells.
Statement II: In the sexual cycle of fungi, meiosis in the zygote results in haploid spores.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. In ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, plasmogamy is not followed at once by karyogamy. A dikaryotic (n + n) stage, the dikaryophase, comes in between, and the two nuclei fuse later in the reproductive structures.
Statement II is correct. The fungal sexual cycle runs plasmogamy → karyogamy → meiosis in the zygote, and meiosis gives haploid spores.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Some ascomycetes are described as coprophilous. This term means that they:
options: Grow on decaying wood in damp places
Live as obligate parasites on plants
questions.explanation:
Coprophilous means 'dung-loving', from the Greek kopros (dung) and philos (loving). Coprophilous fungi grow on dung.
NCERT describes ascomycetes as saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous.
Growth on decaying wood is a decomposer habit, not a coprophilous one.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (fungus) with List-II (class):
List-I
A. Neurospora
B. Ustilago
C. Trichoderma
D. Mucor
List-II
I. Phycomycetes
II. Deuteromycetes
III. Basidiomycetes
IV. Ascomycetes
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. Neurospora is a sac fungus, so it belongs to Ascomycetes (IV).
B. Ustilago (smut) is a club fungus, so it belongs to Basidiomycetes (III).
C. Trichoderma has no known sexual stage, so it belongs to Deuteromycetes (II).
D. Mucor has aseptate, coenocytic hyphae, so it belongs to Phycomycetes (I).
So the correct match is A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Gonyaulax
B. Trypanosoma
C. Nostoc
D. Neurospora
List-II
I. Heterocysts
II. Biochemical and genetic studies
III. Red tides
IV. Sleeping sickness
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A. *Gonyaulax* is a red dinoflagellate. Its blooms colour the sea, causing red tides (III).
B. *Trypanosoma* is a flagellated protozoan that causes sleeping sickness (IV).
C. *Nostoc* is a cyanobacterium that fixes nitrogen in specialised cells called heterocysts (I).
D. *Neurospora* is an ascomycete used extensively in biochemical and genetic studies (II).
The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about protozoans are correct?
(i) Entamoeba is a parasitic amoeboid protozoan.
(ii) All flagellated protozoans are parasitic.
(iii) In ciliated protozoans, the gullet opens to the outside of the cell surface.
(iv) Plasmodium, the malarial parasite, is a flagellated protozoan.
(v) Amoeboid protozoans may live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil.
(vi) Some protozoans are photosynthetic, while others are predators or parasites.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: Entamoeba is a parasitic amoeboid protozoan.
(ii) Incorrect: flagellated protozoans may be free-living or parasitic.
(iii) Correct: in ciliates, the gullet opens to the outside of the cell surface.
(iv) Incorrect: Plasmodium is a sporozoan, not a flagellate.
(v) Correct: amoeboid protozoans live in fresh water, sea water or moist soil.
(vi) Incorrect: all protozoans are heterotrophs, so none is photosynthetic.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Euglena is correct?
options: Its rigid cellulose cell wall keeps its body shape fixed
It has a protein-rich pellicle and two flagella of unequal length
Its pigments are completely different from those of higher plants
It is a strict autotroph and dies when kept in darkness
questions.explanation:
(1) Wrong: Euglena has no cell wall. Its flexible pellicle allows it to change shape.
(2) Correct: It has a protein-rich pellicle and two flagella, one short and one long.
(3) Wrong: Its pigments are identical to those of higher plants.
(4) Wrong: Euglena is not a strict autotroph. In darkness it behaves as a heterotroph, preying on smaller organisms.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): All protozoans obtain their food heterotrophically, either as predators or as parasites.
Reason (R): Protozoans are believed to be primitive relatives of plants.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
Assertion: true. Every protozoan is heterotrophic and lives as a predator or a parasite.
Reason: false. NCERT describes protozoans as primitive relatives of animals, not plants.
Since R is false, options (1), (2) and (4) are ruled out.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Viruses were not given a place in Whittaker's five kingdom classification.
Reason (R): Viruses are non-cellular, and outside a living host cell they exist as an inert crystalline structure.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: Whittaker's five kingdom system makes no mention of acellular agents such as viruses, viroids and prions.
R is true: viruses have no cell structure. Outside a host cell they are inert, crystalline particles, and they behave as living only inside a host.
Because they are non-cellular and not truly living, they could not be placed in any of the five kingdoms of organisms. So R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A diagram shows a virus with a polyhedral head, a collar and a sheath below the head, and several thin tail fibres at the base. Which option correctly gives its usual host and the type of genetic material it typically carries?
questions.explanation:
A polyhedral head, collar, sheath and tail fibres are the typical features of a bacteriophage, such as the T-even phages.
Bacteriophages infect bacteria and usually carry double-stranded DNA, so option (1) fits.
Option (2) is the tempting trap. It describes TMV, a helical, rod-shaped plant virus with ssRNA that has no head or tail fibres.
Option (4) names the right host but the wrong genetic material.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following diseases is NOT caused by a bacterium?
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists cholera, typhoid, tetanus and citrus canker as bacterial diseases.
Citrus canker is a plant disease, but it is still caused by a bacterium. Do not rule it out just because it affects plants.
Mumps is caused by a virus, not a bacterium.
So mumps is the only option that is not bacterial.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans.
Reason (R): The cell walls of diatoms are embedded with silica, which makes them practically indestructible.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans because they are abundant photosynthetic plankton.
R is true. Their walls form two thin overlapping shells embedded with silica, which makes them practically indestructible.
R does not explain A. The silica walls explain the build-up of diatomaceous earth, not their role as producers. That role comes from photosynthesis.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A fungus was long known only from its conidia and was therefore placed in Deuteromycetes. Later, its sexual stage was discovered. In this stage, two somatic cells of different strains fuse, karyogamy and meiosis occur in a single cell, and that cell then bears four spores on its outside. The fungus should now be placed in:
options: Deuteromycetes itself, since conidia are still produced
questions.explanation:
The fungus was in Deuteromycetes only because its sexual (perfect) stage was unknown. Once that stage is found, it moves to its proper class.
In the sexual stage, somatic cells of different strains fuse. Karyogamy and meiosis then occur in one cell, which bears four spores on its outside. This cell is a basidium carrying four exogenous basidiospores, the hallmark of Basidiomycetes.
Ascomycetes form endogenous ascospores inside an ascus, so (1) fails.
Producing conidia does not keep a fungus in Deuteromycetes once its sexual stage is known, so (4) fails.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following organisms completely lack a cell wall, are the smallest living cells known, and can survive without oxygen?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall, are the smallest living cells known, and many survive without oxygen.
Cyanobacteria and methanogens both have cell walls. Methanogens can live without oxygen, but they are not wall-less.
Diatoms have silica-embedded walls.
Only Mycoplasma fits all three features.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The spores of slime moulds possess true walls and can survive for many years even under adverse conditions.
Statement II: The spores of slime moulds are dispersed mainly by water currents.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Slime mould spores have true walls, are extremely resistant, and survive for many years even under adverse conditions.
Statement II is incorrect. These spores are dispersed by air currents, not water currents.
So Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In cyanobacteria such as Nostoc and Anabaena, what is the function of the specialised cells called heterocysts?
options: Storage of excess food as glycogen
Formation of spores during unfavourable conditions
Transfer of DNA from one bacterium to another
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: some cyanobacteria, such as Nostoc and Anabaena, fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialised cells called heterocysts.
Option (3) does not fit, because spore formation is a general bacterial response to unfavourable conditions.
Option (4) does not fit, because DNA transfer is a form of sexual reproduction in bacteria.
Neither of these is the role of heterocysts.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Red tides, in which the sea appears red, are caused by the rapid multiplication of which organism?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax can multiply so rapidly that the sea appears red. This is called a red tide.
So option (3) is correct.
Option (2) is the tempting wrong choice. Nostoc is a cyanobacterium that forms blooms in polluted water bodies, but it does not cause red tides.
Euglena is a euglenoid and Paramoecium is a ciliate protozoan, so neither causes red tides.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (Kingdom) with List-II (Nature of cell wall as per the five-kingdom comparison).
List-I:
A. Monera
B. Protista
C. Fungi
D. Animalia
List-II:
I. Present, with chitin
II. Absent
III. Noncellulosic (polysaccharide + amino acid)
IV. Present in some
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
These matches come from NCERT's five kingdom comparison table.
A. Monera: noncellulosic wall of polysaccharide and amino acid (III).
B. Protista: cell wall present in some members (IV).
C. Fungi: wall present, made of chitin (I).
D. Animalia: no cell wall (II).
Option (2) is the common error because it swaps Monera and Protista.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the comparative table of the five kingdoms, in which kingdom is the cell wall noncellulosic and made of polysaccharide + amino acid?
questions.explanation:
In NCERT's comparison table of the five kingdoms, the Monera cell wall is described as noncellulosic, made of polysaccharide + amino acid (peptidoglycan).
The other kingdoms differ:
- Fungi have walls with chitin.
- Plantae have cellulose walls.
- Protista vary; some have cell walls.
So only Monera matches.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In ascomycetes, conidia are produced exogenously on special hyphae called conidiophores.
Reason (R): In ascomycetes, ascospores are produced endogenously inside sac-like asci.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: ascomycetes reproduce asexually by conidia. These form exogenously, on the outside of special hyphae called conidiophores.
R is true: their sexual spores, ascospores, form endogenously inside sac-like asci.
R does not explain A. It describes sexual spore formation, while A describes asexual spore formation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Whittaker's comparison of the five kingdoms, which kingdom has a non-cellulosic cell wall made of polysaccharide and amino acid?
questions.explanation:
Whittaker's comparison table gives the cell wall type for each kingdom.
Monera has a non-cellulosic wall made of polysaccharide plus amino acid (peptidoglycan).
Fungi have chitin walls, and Plantae have cellulose walls.
In Protista, a cell wall is present only in some members, so it is not the defining feature.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The boundaries of Kingdom Protista are well defined, and all biologists agree on which photosynthetic forms belong to it.
Statement II: Chrysophytes include diatoms and golden algae (desmids), found in both fresh water and marine environments.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement I is false. NCERT says the boundaries of Protista are not well defined. One biologist's 'photosynthetic protistan' may be another's 'plant'.
Statement II is true. Chrysophytes include diatoms and golden algae (desmids). They occur in both fresh water and marine environments.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The body of Euglena is flexible.
Reason (R): Euglenoids lack a cell wall and are instead covered by a protein-rich pellicle.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the body of *Euglena* is flexible.
R is true: euglenoids have no cell wall and are covered by a protein-rich pellicle.
NCERT states directly that the pellicle makes their body flexible. A rigid wall is absent, so the lack of a wall plus the pellicle explains the flexibility.
So R is the correct explanation of A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (scientist) with List-II (contribution):
List-I
(a) Dmitri Ivanowsky (1892)
(b) M.W. Beijerinck (1898)
(c) W.M. Stanley (1935)
(d) T.O. Diener (1971)
List-II
(i) Showed that viruses can be crystallised and the crystals are largely protein
(ii) Discovered a free, low molecular weight RNA infectious agent
(iii) Found that the agent of tobacco mosaic disease passes through bacteria-proof filters
(iv) Named the new pathogen 'virus'
questions.explanation:
(a) Ivanowsky: found that the tobacco mosaic agent passes through bacteria-proof filters, so (iii).
(b) Beijerinck: named the pathogen 'virus', so (iv).
(c) Stanley: showed that viruses can be crystallised and the crystals are largely protein, so (i).
(d) Diener: discovered the free RNA infectious agent (viroid), so (ii).
The common trap is swapping Ivanowsky and Beijerinck.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: All eukaryotic unicellular organisms belong to
questions.explanation:
Kingdom Protista includes all single-celled eukaryotes, such as diatoms, dinoflagellates, euglenoids, slime moulds and protozoans.
Monera and bacteria fail because they are prokaryotes with no nuclear membrane.
Fungi fail because most are multicellular. Yeast is a unicellular exception, so fungi do not include all unicellular eukaryotes.
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 2 (MCQ Q1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: White spots seen on mustard leaves are caused by a parasitic fungus. To which class does this fungus belong?
questions.explanation:
White rust (white spots) on mustard is caused by the parasitic fungus *Albugo*.
NCERT places *Albugo* in Phycomycetes. Members of this class have aseptate, coenocytic mycelium and form zoospores or aplanospores endogenously in sporangia.
The tempting wrong option is Basidiomycetes. That class contains rusts (*Puccinia*) and smuts (*Ustilago*), not the white rust of mustard.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a member of Deuteromycetes?
questions.explanation:
Key fact (NCERT): Alternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma are listed as examples of deuteromycetes.
Agaricus is the mushroom. It belongs to basidiomycetes, because sexual reproduction through basidia and basidiospores is known for it.
So Agaricus is the one that is NOT a deuteromycete.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A marine biologist finds a coastal sea turned red, with many dead fish. Microscopic examination shows huge numbers of a single-celled photosynthetic organism. Its outer wall is made of stiff cellulose plates, and it has two flagella: one longitudinal and one lying in a transverse groove between the plates. Which is the most likely identification and cause of the fish deaths?
options: Diatoms; their silica shells clog the gills of fishes
Dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax; toxins released by their large numbers
Euglenoids; their pellicle makes them predate on fishes
Cyanobacteria; heterocysts release excess nitrogen that poisons fishes
questions.explanation:
Identify the organism: a wall of stiff cellulose plates, plus two flagella (one longitudinal and one in a transverse furrow), marks a dinoflagellate.
Cause of deaths: rapid multiplication of red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax turns the sea red (red tide). Toxins released in such large numbers may even kill fish.
Why not (1): diatoms have silica shells, not cellulose plates, and do not cause red tides.
Euglenoids and cyanobacteria do not fit this wall and flagella description.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Slime moulds can survive unfavourable conditions for many years.
Reason (R): During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates into fruiting bodies that bear spores with true walls, which are extremely resistant.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: slime moulds survive adverse conditions for many years.
R is true: under unfavourable conditions the plasmodium forms fruiting bodies bearing spores with true walls, which are extremely resistant.
R correctly explains A, because these resistant spores are what let the organism persist and later disperse by air. The plasmodium itself does not survive; it forms only under suitable conditions.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The mycelium of Mucor is aseptate and coenocytic.
(ii) Aplanospores of phycomycetes are motile asexual spores.
(iii) In ascomycetes, ascospores are produced exogenously.
(iv) Yeast (Saccharomyces) is a unicellular member of the sac fungi.
(v) In phycomycetes, a zygospore may result from the fusion of morphologically dissimilar gametes.
(vi) Aspergillus and Claviceps have branched, septate mycelium.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. Mucor has aseptate, coenocytic mycelium.
(ii) Incorrect. Aplanospores are non-motile. Zoospores are the motile spores.
(iii) Incorrect. Ascospores are formed endogenously in asci.
(iv) Correct. Yeast is a unicellular sac fungus.
(v) Correct. Phycomycete gametes may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous, so they can be dissimilar.
(vi) Correct. Ascomycetes such as Aspergillus and Claviceps have branched, septate mycelium.
Correct statements = 4.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student examines the gill of a mushroom under a microscope. She sees a cell bearing four spores attached on its outer surface. These spores are:
questions.explanation:
Key fact: The gills of a mushroom (Agaricus) carry basidia. Each basidium bears four basidiospores on its outer surface, which is exogenous formation.
A club-shaped cell with four external spores is therefore a basidium bearing basidiospores.
Ascospores are the tempting wrong option. They form endogenously, inside asci, usually eight per ascus.
Conidia are asexual spores, and zoospores are motile spores of phycomycetes.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the genetic material of viruses is INCORRECT?
options: Viruses that infect plants generally have single-stranded RNA
Bacteriophages are usually double-stranded DNA viruses
Animal viruses may have single- or double-stranded RNA, or double-stranded DNA
Some viruses carry both RNA and DNA, which together make the virus infectious
questions.explanation:
No virus contains both RNA and DNA. Each virus has only one type of nucleic acid, and this genetic material is infectious, so (4) is incorrect.
(1) is true: plant viruses generally have single-stranded RNA.
(2) is true: bacteriophages are usually double-stranded DNA viruses.
(3) is true: animal viruses may have single- or double-stranded RNA, or double-stranded DNA.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT described in NCERT as a symptom of viral infection in plants?
options: White spots on leaves caused by a parasite that produces zoospores
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists these viral symptoms in plants: mosaic formation, leaf rolling and curling, yellowing, vein clearing, dwarfing and stunted growth.
White spots on leaves caused by a zoospore-producing parasite describe Albugo, a phycomycete fungus that causes white rust of mustard. This is not a viral symptom.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following fungi belongs to the class Deuteromycetes?
questions.explanation:
Deuteromycetes (imperfect fungi) are fungi whose sexual stage is unknown. NCERT examples are Alternaria, Colletotrichum and Trichoderma.
Ustilago (smut), Agaricus (mushroom) and Puccinia (rust) are all basidiomycetes.
So only Trichoderma belongs to Deuteromycetes.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Viruses are non-cellular organisms but replicate themselves once they infect the host cell. To which of the following kingdom do viruses belong to?
questions.explanation:
NCERT treats viruses as acellular. They show living properties only inside a host cell and are inert crystalline structures outside it.
Whittaker's five kingdoms (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) contain only cellular organisms. So viruses, viroids and lichens are not included in any kingdom.
Monera is the tempting wrong option, but monerans are true prokaryotic cells with their own metabolism. Viruses are not cells at all.
Answer: (4)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 2 (MCQ Q11)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Holozoic nutrition
(b) Cell wall mainly of cellulose
(c) Cell wall of chitin
(d) Noncellulosic wall of polysaccharide and amino acid
List-II
(i) Monera
(ii) Fungi
(iii) Animalia
(iv) Plantae
questions.explanation:
(a) Holozoic nutrition (ingesting food) is seen in Animalia: a-iii.
(b) A cell wall mainly of cellulose is found in Plantae: b-iv.
(c) A cell wall of chitin is found in Fungi: c-ii.
(d) A noncellulosic wall of polysaccharide and amino acid is found in Monera: d-i.
Only option (1) matches all four pairs.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Most euglenoids are freshwater organisms found in stagnant water.
(ii) The pigments of euglenoids differ from those present in higher plants.
(iii) The plasmodium of a slime mould may grow and spread over several feet.
(iv) Slime moulds form fruiting bodies during favourable conditions.
(v) Slime mould spores are extremely resistant and can survive for many years.
(vi) Euglena has a cellulose cell wall.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: most euglenoids live in fresh stagnant water.
(ii) Incorrect: their pigments are identical to those of higher plants.
(iii) Correct: the plasmodium can spread over several feet.
(iv) Incorrect: fruiting bodies form under unfavourable conditions.
(v) Correct: the walled spores are highly resistant and survive for many years.
(vi) Incorrect: Euglena has a protein-rich pellicle, not a cellulose wall.
Correct statements are (i), (iii) and (v), so the count is 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements about chrysophytes and dinoflagellates:
Statement I: Dinoflagellates usually have two flagella, one lying longitudinally and the other transversely in a furrow between the cellulose wall plates.
Statement II: Red tides are caused by the rapid multiplication of diatoms, and the gritty deposits these diatoms leave behind are used for filtering oils and syrups.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Most dinoflagellates have two flagella. One lies longitudinally and the other transversely, in a furrow between the cellulose wall plates.
Statement II is incorrect. Red tides are caused by the rapid multiplication of red dinoflagellates such as *Gonyaulax*, not diatoms.
The second half of Statement II is true by itself: diatomaceous earth is used for filtering oils and syrups. But the claim as a whole is wrong.
So Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, cells formed after the fusion of two compatible haploid hyphae contain two nuclei each.
Reason (R): In these fungi, karyogamy does not immediately follow plasmogamy.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: when two compatible haploid hyphae fuse in ascomycetes and basidiomycetes, the resulting cells carry two nuclei each. This is the dikaryotic ($n + n$) condition.
R is true: in these fungi, karyogamy (fusion of nuclei) does not follow plasmogamy (fusion of cytoplasm) at once.
R explains A. Because the nuclei do not fuse right away, the two parental nuclei stay separate in each cell, giving the dikaryon. They fuse later to form diploid cells.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A fungus has the following features:
1. Branched, septate mycelium
2. Asexual spores borne exogenously on specialised hyphae
3. Sexual spores formed endogenously inside sac-like cells
4. These sac-like cells are grouped within fruiting bodies
The fungus is most likely:
questions.explanation:
Branched, septate mycelium rules out Rhizopus and Albugo, which have aseptate, coenocytic hyphae.
Asexual spores borne exogenously on special hyphae are conidia on conidiophores.
Sexual spores formed endogenously in sacs are ascospores in asci. Fruiting bodies holding the asci are ascocarps. Together these features identify an ascomycete.
Aspergillus is an ascomycete.
Agaricus fails because its basidiospores form exogenously on a basidium.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which group of protozoans do the marine forms have silica shells on their surface?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: the marine forms of amoeboid protozoans have silica shells on their surface.
Ciliates, flagellates and sporozoans are not described as having silica shells.
A tempting confusion is with diatoms. Diatoms are chrysophytes whose cell walls are embedded with silica, but they are not protozoans.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Archaebacteria can live in habitats such as extremely salty areas and hot springs, where very few other organisms survive.
Reason (R): Archaebacteria have a cell wall structure that differs from that of other bacteria.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Archaebacteria live in harsh habitats such as extremely salty areas (halophiles) and hot springs (thermoacidophiles).
R is true. Their cell wall structure differs from that of other bacteria.
NCERT states that this distinct cell wall is responsible for their survival in extreme conditions.
So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the filamentous cyanobacteria Nostoc and Anabaena, what is the main role of the specialised cells called heterocysts?
options: Storage of reserve food as glycogen
Formation of spores under unfavourable conditions
Secretion of the gelatinous sheath around the colony
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: some cyanobacteria, such as Nostoc and Anabaena, have specialised cells called heterocysts that fix atmospheric nitrogen.
So option (2) is correct.
Option (4) is the tempting wrong choice. The gelatinous sheath does surround cyanobacterial colonies, but heterocysts do not secrete it.
Food storage and spore formation are not the role NCERT gives to heterocysts.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Kingdom Protista places Chlamydomonas and Chlorella in the same kingdom as Amoeba and Paramoecium, although these organisms belonged to different kingdoms in earlier classifications.
Reason (R): In Whittaker's system, organisms are grouped into Protista mainly because they possess a cell wall.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Walled forms (Chlamydomonas, Chlorella) were earlier placed with plants, and wall-less forms (Amoeba, Paramoecium) with animals. Whittaker grouped all of them in Protista.
R is false. Protista unites unicellular eukaryotes whether or not they have a cell wall. Grouping by the presence of a cell wall was the basis of the older 'Plants' grouping.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following diseases are caused by bacteria?
Cholera, Mumps, Typhoid, Malaria, Tetanus, Influenza, Citrus canker, Sleeping sickness
questions.explanation:
Bacterial diseases in the list: cholera, typhoid, tetanus and citrus canker. That makes 4.
Viral diseases: mumps and influenza.
Protozoan diseases: malaria (caused by Plasmodium) and sleeping sickness (caused by Trypanosoma).
So 4 of the 8 diseases are bacterial.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about Basidiomycetes are correct?
(i) Asexual spores are generally not found.
(ii) Sex organs are absent; plasmogamy occurs by fusion of two somatic cells of different strains.
(iii) Basidiospores are produced endogenously inside the basidium.
(iv) Karyogamy and meiosis in the basidium produce four basidiospores.
(v) The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: asexual spores are generally absent. Vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common.
(ii) Correct: sex organs are absent. Plasmogamy occurs by fusion of two vegetative (somatic) cells of different strains.
(iii) Incorrect: basidiospores are produced exogenously on the basidium, not inside it.
(iv) Correct: karyogamy and meiosis in the basidium give four basidiospores.
(v) Incorrect: the mycelium is branched and septate. An aseptate, coenocytic mycelium belongs to phycomycetes.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which sequence correctly describes the sexual cycle of Agaricus?
options: Fusion of gametes from sex organs → karyogamy → dikaryon → meiosis → four ascospores
Fusion of two somatic cells of different strains → dikaryotic stage → karyogamy in basidium → meiosis → four basidiospores
Fusion of two somatic cells → karyogamy immediately → meiosis in zygospore → many basidiospores
Plasmogamy of motile gametes → dikaryotic stage → meiosis → karyogamy → four basidiospores
questions.explanation:
*Agaricus* is a basidiomycete, so it has no sex organs.
Plasmogamy happens by fusion of two somatic cells (vegetative hyphae) of different strains. This gives a dikaryotic stage.
Karyogamy then takes place in the basidium, followed by meiosis. Four basidiospores result, so option (2) is correct.
(1) is wrong because it describes ascospores and sex organs. (3) is wrong because it mentions a zygospore. (4) is wrong because it mentions motile gametes and puts meiosis before karyogamy.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Basidiomycetes reproduce sexually even though they lack sex organs.
Reason (R): In basidiomycetes, plasmogamy is brought about by the fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Basidiomycetes have no sex organs, yet they reproduce sexually: plasmogamy, then karyogamy and meiosis in the basidium.
R is true. NCERT states that plasmogamy occurs by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes.
R explains A. Because sex organs are absent, somatic fusion is how sexual reproduction begins. The resulting dikaryon gives rise to the basidium.
So both are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Euglena, the body remains flexible because instead of a cell wall it possesses a:
options: Silica-embedded shell made of two overlapping halves
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: euglenoids lack a cell wall. Instead they have a protein-rich layer called the pellicle, which keeps the body flexible.
The other options belong to different groups. Silica shells with two overlapping halves are found in diatoms. Stiff cellulose plates are found in dinoflagellates. Chitinous walls are found in fungi.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: With respect to fungal sexual cycle, choose the correct sequence of events
questions.explanation:
Sexual reproduction in fungi has three steps in a fixed order.
Step 1, Plasmogamy: the protoplasms of two motile or non-motile gametes fuse.
Step 2, Karyogamy: the two nuclei fuse to form a diploid zygote nucleus.
Step 3, Meiosis: the zygote divides by meiosis to give haploid spores.
Options starting with karyogamy or meiosis are wrong. Nuclei cannot fuse before the cytoplasms fuse, and meiosis needs a diploid nucleus first.
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 2 (MCQ Q10)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sleeping sickness is caused by a parasitic protozoan that belongs to which group?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: flagellated protozoans are either free-living or parasitic. The parasitic Trypanosoma causes sleeping sickness.
The most tempting wrong choice is Plasmodium, a sporozoan. It causes malaria, not sleeping sickness.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Mycoplasma can survive in the absence of oxygen.
Reason (R): Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that Mycoplasma can survive without oxygen.
R is true: Mycoplasma completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known.
Living without oxygen depends on the organism's metabolism. It has nothing to do with whether a cell wall is present.
So R does not explain A.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Bacteria reproduce mainly by fission and may form spores under unfavourable conditions.
Statement II: The sexual reproduction of bacteria involves fusion of male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: bacteria reproduce mainly by fission and form spores under unfavourable conditions.
Statement II is incorrect: bacteria do not form gametes or a diploid zygote.
Their 'sort of sexual reproduction' is only a primitive transfer of DNA from one bacterium to another.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which group of organisms is described in NCERT as the chief 'producers' in the oceans?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: diatoms belong to the chrysophytes, are photosynthetic, and are the chief 'producers' in the oceans.
So option (2) is correct.
Option (1) is the tempting wrong choice. Dinoflagellates are also mostly marine and photosynthetic, but NCERT gives the chief producer title only to diatoms.
Slime moulds are saprophytic, so they cannot be producers.
Euglenoids are mostly freshwater organisms.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In members of ascomycetes such as Penicillium, how are the asexual spores produced?
options: Sporangiospores produced endogenously in a sporangium
Basidiospores produced exogenously on a basidium
questions.explanation:
In ascomycetes, the asexual spores are conidia. They form exogenously on special mycelium called conidiophores.
Option (2) is tempting because ascospores are found in ascomycetes. However, they are sexual spores formed endogenously in asci.
Sporangiospores (option 1) are typical of phycomycetes.
Basidiospores (option 4) belong to basidiomycetes.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The white spots seen on mustard leaves are caused by a parasitic fungus that belongs to phycomycetes. Which fungus is this?
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives Albugo as the parasitic phycomycete that causes white rust (white spots) on mustard.
Puccinia (rust) and Ustilago (smut) are basidiomycetes.
Claviceps (ergot) is an ascomycete.
So only Albugo is a phycomycete.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about cyanobacteria are correct?
(i) They may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous.
(ii) Their colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath.
(iii) They often form blooms in polluted water bodies.
(iv) All cyanobacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen.
(v) They are eukaryotic algae placed under Protista.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: cyanobacteria may be unicellular, colonial or filamentous.
(ii) Correct: their colonies are generally surrounded by a gelatinous sheath.
(iii) Correct: they often form blooms in polluted water bodies.
(iv) Incorrect: only some, such as Nostoc and Anabaena, fix nitrogen in heterocysts.
(v) Incorrect: they are prokaryotic eubacteria placed under Monera, not Protista.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Kingdom Monera is INCORRECT?
options: The cell wall of monerans is noncellulosic, made of polysaccharide and amino acid
Bacteria are structurally simple but very complex in behaviour
Archaebacteria differ from eubacteria mainly in completely lacking a cell wall
Methanogens occur both in marshy areas and in the gut of ruminant animals
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT describes the moneran cell wall as noncellulosic, made of polysaccharide and amino acid.
(2) Correct: bacteria are structurally simple but very complex in behaviour.
(3) Incorrect: archaebacteria do have a cell wall. They differ from eubacteria in the structure of that wall. Complete absence of a cell wall is the feature of Mycoplasma.
(4) Correct: methanogens live in marshy areas and in the gut of ruminants.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which scientist showed that the extract of infected tobacco plants could infect healthy plants, and called this infectious fluid 'Contagium vivum fluidum'?
questions.explanation:
In 1898, M.W. Beijerinck showed that the extract of infected tobacco plants could infect healthy plants. He called this fluid Contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid).
Ivanowsky (1892) is the tempting option. He only showed that the agent passed through bacteria-proof filters.
Stanley crystallised viruses, and Diener discovered viroids.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: With respect to mode of nutrition, the vast majority of bacteria are:
questions.explanation:
Some bacteria are autotrophs. These may be photosynthetic or chemosynthetic.
However, the vast majority of bacteria are heterotrophs. They depend on other organisms or on dead organic matter for food.
Autotrophy is therefore true of only a minority of bacteria.
Holozoic nutrition means ingesting food, which is typical of animals, not bacteria.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Difference between Virus and Viroid is
options: Absence of protein coat in viroid but present in virus
Presence of low molecular weight RNA in virus but absent in viroid
questions.explanation:
Viroids were discovered by T.O. Diener as the cause of potato spindle tuber disease.
A viroid is free RNA that lacks the protein coat found in viruses, so statement (a) is correct.
The RNA of viroids is of low molecular weight. Statement (b) reverses this by giving low molecular weight RNA to viruses, so it is wrong.
Since (b) is wrong, 'Both a and b' fails.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 2 (MCQ Q9)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In members of Kingdom Animalia, food reserves are stored mainly as:
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that members of Animalia store reserve food as glycogen or fat.
Starch is the reserve food of plants, so (1) is the tempting wrong option.
Cellulose (plant walls) and chitin (fungal walls) are structural materials, not food reserves.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are groups of archaebacteria?
Halophiles, Cyanobacteria, Thermoacidophiles, Mycoplasma, Methanogens, Nostoc
questions.explanation:
Halophiles: archaebacteria (salty areas).
Thermoacidophiles: archaebacteria (hot springs).
Methanogens: archaebacteria (marshes and ruminant gut).
Cyanobacteria and Nostoc: photosynthetic eubacteria, not archaebacteria.
Mycoplasma: organisms without a cell wall, not archaebacteria.
Total = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The five kingdom classification was proposed by
questions.explanation:
R.H. Whittaker proposed the five kingdom classification in 1969.
His kingdoms are Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.
He based them on cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships.
Linnaeus is the tempting wrong option. He gave the two kingdom system (Plantae and Animalia), not five kingdoms.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 2 (MCQ Q2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: With reference to Whittaker's five kingdom comparison, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Monera have a noncellulosic cell wall made of polysaccharide and amino acid
Fungi have a cell wall containing chitin and show multicellular or loose tissue body organisation
All members of Protista possess a cell wall, as they were earlier placed among algae
Animalia lack a cell wall and show a tissue/organ/organ-system level of organisation
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Monera have a noncellulosic cell wall made of polysaccharide and amino acid.
(2) Correct: fungi have a chitin cell wall and a multicellular or loose-tissue body.
(3) Incorrect: only some protists have a cell wall. Protozoans such as Amoeba and Paramoecium lack one, and they were earlier placed among animals, not algae.
(4) Correct: animals lack a cell wall and show a tissue, organ or organ-system level of organisation.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student examines a sample from a polluted pond showing a bloom. Under the microscope the organism is prokaryotic, has a rigid cell wall, is photosynthetic, and forms filaments enclosed in a gelatinous sheath. A few distinctive specialised cells are seen at intervals along each filament. Which inference is correct?
options: It is a golden alga of Kingdom Protista with silica walls
It lacks a cell wall and is related to Mycoplasma
It is a cyanobacterium like Nostoc, and the specialised cells can fix atmospheric nitrogen
It is an archaebacterium whose wall structure allows survival in hot springs
questions.explanation:
The clues together point to a cyanobacterium such as Nostoc:
- prokaryotic, with a rigid cell wall
- photosynthetic
- filaments enclosed in a gelatinous sheath
- forms blooms in polluted water
The specialised cells along the filament are heterocysts, which fix atmospheric nitrogen.
Golden algae are eukaryotic, so (1) is wrong. Mycoplasma lack a cell wall, so (2) is wrong. Archaebacteria do not show this photosynthetic, heterocyst-bearing form, so (4) is wrong.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Aplanospores of phycomycetes are non-motile and are produced endogenously in a sporangium
Morels and truffles are edible ascomycetes considered delicacies
Ascocarps are fruiting bodies in which the conidia of sac fungi are arranged
Members of phycomycetes may occur as obligate parasites on plants
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. Aplanospores are non-motile spores formed endogenously in sporangia.
(2) Correct. Morels and truffles are edible ascomycetes valued as delicacies.
(3) Incorrect. Ascocarps hold asci containing the sexual ascospores. Conidia are asexual spores borne exogenously on conidiophores.
(4) Correct. Some phycomycetes, such as Albugo, are obligate plant parasites.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the three-domain system mentioned in NCERT?
options: It divides Kingdom Protista into two domains and places all prokaryotes in the third domain
It divides Kingdom Monera into two domains, places the remaining eukaryotic kingdoms in the third domain, and thus gives a six kingdom classification
It merges Fungi and Plantae into one domain, giving a four kingdom classification
It divides Kingdom Animalia into vertebrates and invertebrates, giving a six kingdom classification
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: the three-domain system divides Kingdom Monera (the prokaryotes) into two domains. All the remaining eukaryotic kingdoms go into the third domain.
Monera becomes two kingdoms and the four eukaryotic kingdoms remain, which gives a six kingdom classification.
Option (1) is wrong because Protista is eukaryotic and is not split.
Options (3) and (4) do not match NCERT.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Diatomaceous earth
B. Red tide
C. Plankton
D. Transverse furrow
List-II
(i) Organisms that float passively in water currents
(ii) Gritty deposit used in polishing and filtering oils and syrups
(iii) Groove between wall plates that holds one flagellum of a dinoflagellate
(iv) Rapid multiplication of Gonyaulax
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation:
A – (ii): Diatomaceous earth is a gritty deposit used in polishing and in filtering oils and syrups.
B – (iv): Red tide is caused by rapid multiplication of red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax.
C – (i): Plankton are organisms that float passively in water currents.
D – (iii): In dinoflagellates, one flagellum lies in the transverse furrow between the wall plates.
Only option (1) gives this matching.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Anabaena
(B) Mycoplasma
(C) Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria
(D) Heterotrophic bacteria
List-II:
(I) Smallest living cells known
(II) Oxidise ammonia, nitrites and nitrates for ATP production
(III) Conversion of milk into curd
(IV) Nitrogen fixation in heterocysts
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A-IV: Anabaena fixes nitrogen in specialised cells called heterocysts.
B-I: Mycoplasma are the smallest living cells known.
C-II: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria oxidise ammonia, nitrites and nitrates and use the released energy to make ATP.
D-III: Heterotrophic bacteria such as Lactobacillus convert milk into curd.
This matches option (1).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which ascomycete is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work?
questions.explanation:
NCERT names Neurospora as the sac fungus used extensively in biochemical and genetic work.
The other options are also ascomycetes, but the text links them to different points: Aspergillus and Penicillium as common examples, Claviceps as a well-known ascomycete, and Saccharomyces as a unicellular sac fungus (yeast).
Only Neurospora is the one NCERT highlights for research.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Halophiles
B. Thermoacidophiles
C. Methanogens
D. Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria
List-II
I. Hot springs
II. Oxidise ammonia, nitrites and nitrates for ATP production
III. Extremely salty areas
IV. Marshy areas and the gut of ruminants
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A. Halophiles live in extremely salty areas, so A–III.
B. Thermoacidophiles live in hot springs, so B–I.
C. Methanogens live in marshy areas and the gut of ruminants, so C–IV.
D. Chemosynthetic autotrophs oxidise inorganic substances such as ammonia, nitrites and nitrates to produce ATP, so D–II.
The matching set is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following diseases are caused by viruses?
Mumps, Typhoid, Small pox, Citrus canker, Herpes, Influenza, Tetanus, AIDS, Mad cow disease
questions.explanation:
Viral: mumps, small pox, herpes, influenza and AIDS. That makes 5.
Bacterial: typhoid, citrus canker and tetanus.
Mad cow disease (BSE) is caused by a prion, an abnormally folded protein, so it is not viral.
Total viral diseases = 5.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Zygospore
(B) Ascocarp
(C) Conidiophore
(D) Sporangium
List-II
(I) Fruiting body in which asci are arranged
(II) Special mycelium bearing exogenously formed asexual spores
(III) Structure formed by fusion of two gametes in phycomycetes
(IV) Structure in which zoospores or aplanospores form endogenously
Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation:
A-III: A zygospore forms by fusion of two gametes in phycomycetes.
B-I: An ascocarp is the fruiting body in which asci are arranged.
C-II: A conidiophore is special mycelium bearing exogenous conidia.
D-IV: Zoospores (motile) or aplanospores (non-motile) form endogenously in a sporangium.
This gives A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophs because they possess:
options: Chlorophyll a, similar to that of green plants
Chloroplasts bounded by a double membrane
Pigments identical to those of red dinoflagellates
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) as having chlorophyll a, similar to green plants. This lets them photosynthesise like plants.
Bacteriochlorophyll is found in other photosynthetic bacteria, not as the sole pigment of cyanobacteria. So (2) is wrong.
Cyanobacteria are prokaryotes and have no membrane-bound chloroplasts. So (3) is wrong.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 2 · Biological Classification
